title: So Good They Can’t Ignore You

questions.q: According to Cal Newport, what does whether you love your work mostly depend on?
a: Your expertise and experience
Your innate talent and personality
How much your employer pays you
Whether you found your one true passion
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that loving your job is mostly a product of expertise and experience, not of discovering a pre-existing passion.

questions.q: Self-determination theory says intrinsic motivation comes from which three things?
a: Autonomy, competence and relatedness
Salary, status and job security
Passion, talent and luck
Freedom, competition and recognition
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists autonomy, competence and relatedness as the three sources of intrinsic motivation.

questions.q: Instead of asking what you want, what question does the summary say you should ask about your job?
a: What value can I bring to my job?
How quickly can I get promoted here?
What would my ideal career look like?
Am I following my true calling?
questions.why: Lesson 2 blames job unhappiness on asking what you want rather than what value you can bring to your work.

questions.q: What kind of practice does the summary recommend for building autonomy and competence?
a: Deliberate practice that keeps you in a state of flow
Repetitive practice that keeps you comfortably busy
Practice only in areas you already excel at
Practice that avoids any risk of frustration
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes deliberate practice as work hard enough to stretch you but not so hard that frustration takes over.

questions.q: Why does the summary suggest turning down a raise or promotion?
a: To keep the control over your time and work that you earned
To signal to your boss that you are underpaid
To free up money for the company’s other employees
To avoid the extra stress that more money brings
questions.why: Lesson 3 warns that rewards like raises are used to take back control, so refusing them protects your hard-won autonomy.
